topics.headline: personal-to-communal link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yaqub’s personal trust is coordinated directly with a general command to trust.
topics.reason: The connector links {{ar:عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi tawakkaltu}}) with the following {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}})-fronted command clause.

words.gloss_range: second fronted prepositional complement with the same divine referent
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) repeats the same fronted object of trust before the command. The repeated pronoun keeps God constant while the person shifts from “I trusted” to “let the trusters trust,” creating the local refrain of the tawakkul climax.

topics.headline: repeated fronted trust object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the universal command begins with the same object of reliance as Yaqub’s personal statement.
topics.reason: The second pronoun resolves to the same divine antecedent and supplies the complement of {{ar:يَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:yatawakkali}}).

words.gloss_range: consequential particle leading into the jussive command
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the final command consequential. Because judgment belongs only to God and Yaqub has trusted Him, the speech now moves into an injunction for those who trust.

topics.headline: therefore into command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final command follows as a consequence of divine judgment and Yaqub’s trust.
topics.reason: The particle combines with lām al-amr before the jussive verb and marks the move from testimony to prescription.

words.gloss_range: jussive command lām forming an indirect imperative
words.prose: {{ar:لْ}} ({{tr:l}}) is lām al-amr, the command marker that makes {{ar:يَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:yatawakkali}}) a third-person injunction. Joined to {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}), it compresses consequence and command into the recited cluster before the verb, and it opens the instruction beyond the sons to the named trusters.

topics.headline: third-person command marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the command broadens beyond the sons into a rule for the class of trusters.
topics.reason: The lām al-amr governs {{ar:يَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:yatawakkali}}), producing a third-person jussive injunction.

words.gloss_range: Form V jussive verb commanding reliance upon God
words.prose: {{ar:يَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:yatawakkali}}) is the conversion point: Yaqub’s completed {{ar:تَوَكَّلْتُ}} ({{tr:tawakkaltu}}) becomes a jussive command. The singular verb before a plural subject is normal verb-first grammar, and the fronted {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) keeps the command fixed on God. The formula resonates with trust-command passages such as 9:51, 14:11, and the near-verbatim 14:12.
words.root_gloss_range: delegating, relying, entrusting affairs, and appointing a trustee; here Form V selects self-entrusting reliance in command mood

topics.headline: jussive self-entrusting command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Yaqub’s completed trust becomes a commanded practice for trusters.
topics.reason: The verb is jussive under lām al-amr, takes the fronted {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) complement, and precedes its plural subject in normal verb-first order.

words.gloss_range: definite Form V active participle naming the trusters
words.prose: {{ar:الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ}} ({{tr:al-mutawakkilūna}}) closes the ayah by turning reliance into identity. The subject and command fold into each other: let the trusters trust. As a definite plural Form V active participle, the word completes the {{ar:و ك ل}} ({{tr:w-k-l}}) triplet from act to command to class, and it matches the near-verbatim closing formula in 14:12.
words.root_gloss_range: one who relies or commits affairs to another; here the definite plural participle names the class defined by reliance upon God

topics.headline: trust as named identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah ends by naming a community through the very act it commands.
topics.reason: The participle is the explicit subject of the jussive verb; definiteness and Form V make the command name its own audience.
